title: Buttons on the Item
summary: Put a button on the item itself, drag it where it goes, watch it ride the pose, and see it from behind.

steps.title: Step 1: Put Reach on the Forearm
text: 1. In the Kneady tab's tree, click Reach.
3. Hover the forearm: Reach has left the column for the front of the forearm - faint where FK, in front of it, covers it.
The arm is as The Look of Your Buttons left it. A button on the item sits at its own point on the surface and stays there as you orbit and pose; In Row puts it back in the column.

steps.title: Step 2: Place It by the Wrist
text: 1. Click Viewport Edit, then Place on Surface under it.
2. Drag Reach onto the side of the forearm by the wrist, and let go.
3. Press Enter to keep it, then click Viewport Edit again to leave it.
Place on Surface holds the region's buttons on screen while you drag them, and Blender's snapping works as it does for G. Dropped on the column, a button goes back into it; Esc puts everything back.

media.label: In the Kneady tab, then on the forearm

steps.title: Step 3: It Rides the Arm
text: 1. Drag Reach: the hand moves the arm - and Reach stays on the forearm.
A button on the item rides the bone that moves its part of the item, so it keeps its place on the surface however the arm is posed.

steps.title: Step 4: Seen From Behind
text: 1. Click Forearm in the tree, and set Behind to Ghost Behind.
2. Orbit round the arm - drag with the middle mouse button - until Reach's side faces away: Reach shows faint through it.
Hide Behind, the default, hides a button on the item when its side faces away from you; Show Behind always shows it as it is. Behind is one setting for all of a region's buttons on the item.

media.label: In the Kneady tab, then in the view
